Edit: And to answer your question, the thing about the trenches is that they were all essentially a natural human response to the constant shelling. The air above ground was full of death in the form of flying shrapnel, so they dug in. This created a massive front, stretching hundreds of miles and made it almost impossible to flank or break through when you add the barbed wire and machine gun nests. Most of WWI was a giant stalemate, until tanks and planes became more widely used.
